item.observed: A timed-out send is retried on the next poll although the first post may have landed.
item.title: Followers can receive duplicate deal posts after a Telegram timeout — the new account and bot send paths release the claim and retry even when the first send may have succeeded

item.observed: One failed channel resolve plus one successful send leaves the failed channel unposted.
item.title: A temporarily unreachable destination permanently misses a deal even when the other channel posts it — failed channel resolution is dropped from the send plan without scheduling a retry

item.observed: One successful conversion sends; a second failed conversion is released but never retried.
item.title: Followers permanently miss one product from a multi-product source post when only its conversion fails — the successful product makes the reader finish without retrying the failed one

item.observed: A restart after cursor advancement loses the in-flight deal and its retry.
item.title: Deals being processed at a restart can be permanently missed — the durable source cursor advances before processing finishes and the retry queue exists only in memory

item.observed: Eleven missed posts leave older posts behind the advanced cursor; posts over 3 min are skipped.
item.title: Busy or briefly disconnected source channels lose eligible deals — the safety poll retrieves only the newest ten and discards messages older than three minutes

item.observed: A successful direct conversion still waits for cleanAffiliate to finish opening the short URL.
item.title: The operator's direct-short-link speed switch cannot avoid the redirect delay — the reader waits for all short links to open before starting duplicate checks or using the converted link

item.observed: A failed first branch before 0.9s resolves immediately; the later Sankmo answer is ignored.
item.title: A deal can fail despite Sankmo later converting it — the hedge resolves the first failure before its delayed fallback has started

item.observed: A late reply to request A can be accepted as the converted link for request B.
item.title: Followers can be sent to the wrong product after a slow Sankmo conversion — replies are matched only by message order, not to the request that produced them

item.observed: A user channel post with a recently reader-posted link is ignored for 10 minutes.
item.title: A genuine channel repost escapes conversion and duplicate handling — the webhook mistakes any post containing recently reader-marked URLs for the reader's own post

item.observed: An arbitrary reader_post_bot value is saved and can fall back to the converter bot.
item.title: The operator can save a nonexistent sender and unknowingly post from another bot — settings never checks the selected destination ID before committing

item.observed: A deleted or tokenless selected bot silently uses the converter bot instead.
item.title: Reader posts use a different bot than the operator selected after that bot is removed — missing selected destinations silently fall back to the converter token

item.observed: A failed redirect leaves fkrt.site classified as Flipkart and sent to conversion.
item.title: Unresolved source affiliate short links can be reposted without identifying the product — cleanLink swallows redirect failures and the reader accepts the original short URL as a product

item.observed: A 'Deal price:' line leaves price at zero, excluding even ₹5,000 deals from Deltfetch.
item.title: Valid expensive deals are omitted from the high-price channel and their posts lack prices — the reader recognizes only exact Price, Selling Price or Discounted Price line formats

item.observed: total_ms is send time minus Telegram message time, not minus server read time.
item.title: The operator cannot measure the reader's processing time against the two-second target — status and history include source delivery delay in their only total

item.observed: The reader tab has no recent duration list or sent count and reports only the last post.
item.title: The operator cannot assess reader speed over a run — the reader status exposes only one in-memory last-send sample and no post count

item.observed: Sender options show names only, without account connection or missing-token status.
item.title: The operator cannot tell which posting choices are disconnected before enabling the reader — the sender selector renders names without readiness information

item.observed: After the third temporary failure the reader drops the retry and keeps the message seen.
item.title: A prolonged temporary converter or Telegram outage permanently loses the affected source deal — the new retry queue discards it after two retries instead of recovering when service returns

item.observed: An in-flight conversion can send after the reader is switched off.
item.title: The operator can still get new channel posts after turning the reader off — stopping removes the timer but does not cancel or recheck in-flight posting jobs

item.observed: last_read, last_sent and last_error reset to null after a process restart.
item.title: The operator loses the reader's last activity and failure history after a restart — status timestamps and errors exist only in process memory

item.observed: A no-product or unsupported conversion is logged but does not update last_error.
item.title: The reader status hides failed conversions — the no-product and unsupported-link branches return after logging without recording last_error

item.observed: The same product gets different claim keys when the destination sender changes.
item.title: Followers receive a repeated product when the operator switches posting accounts or bots — duplicate claims are keyed by the sender token as well as the channel

item.observed: Every queued Sankmo request waits 1.5s since the previous send, even after it has replied.
item.title: Back-to-back deals wait behind Sankmo despite instant replies — the conversion queue still imposes a fixed 1.5-second spacing between sends

item.observed: A hedge remains queued after ExtraPe wins, delaying later Sankmo conversions up to 15s.
item.title: Later deals miss the speed target after ExtraPe wins a race — the losing Sankmo conversion continues in the single serial queue instead of being cancelled

item.observed: Destination Test always sends with d.bot_token, regardless of the selected reader sender.
item.title: The operator cannot test whether the selected spare account can post to a destination — the Test button always sends through that row's bot

item.observed: Bot posts show 'by bot'; status has no poster field with the selected bot's name.
item.title: The operator cannot identify which bot sent the last reader post — status stores the generic word 'bot' instead of the bot's name

item.observed: An existing saved reader_post_bot='converter' overrides the new account default.
item.title: An existing operator can keep posting with the old bot despite choosing the spare account — the new default never migrates the previously saved converter selection

item.observed: After restart the in-memory exemption is lost; a delayed reader post can be deleted as a repeat.
item.title: Followers can lose a reader post after a restart — the webhook's exemption is process-local and a delayed update is then deleted against the reader's own duplicate claim

item.observed: An already sent product can be claimed again as soon as the repeat window expires.
item.title: Followers receive the same product again after the repeat window — reader deduplication expires after the configurable 5–60 minutes instead of retaining a per-destination sent record

item.observed: A rejected source photo causes the entire deal send to fail rather than retrying as text.
item.title: Photo-mode followers miss a deal when Telegram rejects its image — the reader has no sendMessage fallback after sendPhoto fails

item.observed: Destination rows have no Add or Remove control.
item.title: The operator cannot add or remove reader destinations — the settings form renders only existing rows and provides no add or delete controls

item.observed: reader_try_short=null is discarded and other supplied settings are saved.
item.title: Invalid reader settings can be partially saved instead of rejected — null values are discarded before boolean validation and other fields are committed

item.observed: A failed destination list request hides saved bot options and leaves no matching select value.
item.title: The operator can mistake the selected bot for the spare account when the bot list fails to load — the request error is swallowed and the select has no option for the saved value

item.observed: Status uses the first successful destination in configuration order, not the last confirmation.
item.title: The operator sees the wrong total for posting to both channels — the status reports the first configured successful destination's time even when the other confirmed later

item.observed: With reader enabled and no stored session, last_error remains null and status says 'Not connected yet'.
item.title: The operator receives no reader error when the chosen spare account is signed out — startup silently skips a missing Telegram session

item.observed: A failed cache lookup after claiming makes the retry treat an unsent product as a repeat.
item.title: A brief database error can permanently suppress an unposted deal — product claims are not released when parallel conversion or another destination claim rejects

item.observed: converter_logs insert failures are swallowed after a successful send.
item.title: The operator loses the timing and history of successfully posted deals during a database error — the reader silently ignores log insertion failures

item.observed: A double click or repeated add can save duplicate Telegram destination rows.
item.title: Operators can add duplicate Telegram channels and post deals multiple times — Add channel stays enabled during the request and the server has no uniqueness guard

item.observed: Negative or over-100 discounts and arbitrary categories are accepted for destinations.
item.title: A channel can silently miss or receive unintended deals — destination creation and editing do not validate discount range or allowed categories

item.observed: An invalid minimum price is saved as 0 and duplicate normalized channel names are accepted.
item.title: Invalid prices are silently saved as zero and duplicate destination names remain — reader validation coerces invalid values and never deduplicates normalized chats

item.observed: A deal posted to two channels generates two converted history rows for the same link.
item.title: Operators see the same conversion multiple times in history — the reader writes one converted-link row per destination and the history endpoint returns all of them

item.observed: If product A is a repeat, the post can show A's title and price above fresh product B's link.
item.title: Followers can see one product's title and price attached to a different product's link — per-channel link filtering reuses a single parse of the whole multi-product message

item.observed: In a two-product message Deltfetch filters both products by the first parsed price.
item.title: Deltfetch can miss an expensive product or receive a below-threshold product from a multi-product deal — the reader applies one source-wide price before filtering individual links

item.observed: An ExtraPe short-link refusal can wait through other short-link providers before resolved retry.
item.title: A rejected short link can delay a deal far beyond the speed target — the reader awaits the entire direct-link fallback chain before converting the already resolved product URL

item.observed: Saving sources during startup can leave the reader watching the old source list indefinitely.
item.title: The operator can save new source channels yet the reader keeps watching the old ones — restartReader returns while the previous startup is still attaching its settings

item.observed: Any non-Telegram URL in a Sankmo reply is accepted as the converted product link.
item.title: Followers can receive an unrelated or non-earning link when Sankmo includes one in its reply — the reader accepts the first URL without validating it against the requested product

item.observed: An 8-second poll starts another tick even if the previous tick is still running.
item.title: The reader starts overlapping source-read cycles when processing is slow — the eight-second interval launches tick without waiting for the previous cycle

item.observed: Source status records attach success but no per-source last read or polling failure.
item.title: Operators cannot see which source has stopped being read — channel health records resolution at startup but never records each source's last read time or poll result

item.observed: With the reader off, status says 'Switched off' rather than the saved account's connection.
item.title: The operator sees their Telegram account as disconnected after switching off the reader — status uses the live reader connection instead of the persisted login

item.observed: Before the first reader startup, status returns no stored source list or Telegram user.
item.title: The operator cannot see saved source channels or the Telegram user while the reader is off — status returns process-local startup defaults instead of reading stored configuration

item.observed: After one successful status load, later polling failures leave the old status visible.
item.title: The operator sees stale reader status as current when polling fails — the polling error is hidden after initial data has loaded

item.observed: A slow duplicate claim is included in service_ms and displayed as converter time.
item.title: The operator can blame the converter for a slow database or channel lookup — history records the parallel claim-and-conversion wall time as converter time

item.observed: A source post without 'supercoin' defaults to 'Flipkart Deal', not 'Supercoin Deals'.
item.title: Followers see the wrong default caption on ordinary source posts — the formatter substitutes the store name when no SuperCoin text is present

item.observed: A deal below every destination's minimum is recorded as 'failed: No channel takes this price'.
item.title: The operator sees a normal price-filtered deal as a failed conversion — the reader logs every zero-destination result with failed status

item.observed: A bot token containing only spaces is saved as an empty token with a success toast.
item.title: The operator can create an unusable bot or erase an existing token while being told it was saved — destination token validation runs before trimming
